# Measuring AI research automation: eight receipts are not eight autonomous discoveries

An AI research laboratory can generate an impressive stream of commits, reports and experiment results without being able to answer a simple question: how much research can it actually complete without routine human work? Counting artifacts alone does not answer that question. We tested a small evidence-accounting implementation on eight consecutive research topics from Anicca's own development history.

![Cover: eight research receipts, zero confirmed independent acceptances, automation rate unknown](/assets/research/ac02-cover.svg)

## What other laboratories measure

OpenAI's November 18, 2026 [Research acceleration: The jagged frontier](https://openai.com/index/research-acceleration-jagged-frontier/) reports uneven estimated success without human intervention across internal research tasks: monitoring runs reached 79%, technical questions 72%, launching runs 35%, building evaluation or RL environments 29%, and inference/serving implementation 25%. These are the laboratory's estimates for its own workflows, not universal task probabilities. A single aggregate can conceal the bottleneck that prevents an experiment from finishing.

Anthropic's [R&D Automation Index](https://www.anthropic.com/institute/measuring-pace-of-ai-development) starts with a taxonomy of research work, estimates the AI contribution on a six-level scale, and weights categories by person-time. Its August 2026 snapshot reports that AI leads 26% of the weighted work. Leading includes human supervision; it is not evidence of full autonomy. METR's [task-completion time horizons](https://metr.org/time-horizons/) measure the expert-human task duration at which an agent attains a given success probability. Human baseline duration, human intervention time and the agent's wall-clock duration are distinct quantities. METR [explicitly cautions](https://metr.org/notes/2026-01-22-time-horizon-limitations/) against converting horizons directly into research speedups.

![Diagram: separate research receipt, independent acceptance, human labor and cost](/assets/research/ac02-method.svg)

## An evidence contract for a research task

Assign each research task a stable ID before running it. Record the intended outcome, fixed evaluation conditions, attempts including failure, and where to inspect the artifacts. An independent reviewer assesses whether the planned outcome was achieved. Record active human minutes, including setup, corrections and verification, separately from agent runtime. Attribute actual costs; a missing bill is not evidence of zero cost. Required legal or safety oversight is not discarded to make an autonomy metric look better.

Let A be independent acceptance and H observed human labor minutes. A task qualifies for operational autonomy under this deliberately strict diagnostic when A is true and H is zero. Let P be the number of definite successes, F the number of definite failures (acceptance false or positive human minutes), and N the number of due tasks. Missing evidence leaves the rest unknown. The compatible autonomy interval is [P/N, (N−F)/N]. A point estimate is returned only if every task's outcome is determined. This is a partial-identification bound, not a confidence interval; even a narrow bound on a selected sample would not establish generalization. A valid human-time-weighted index additionally requires comparable baseline durations and coverage of the target task population.

## What we ran

We fixed eight consecutive topic IDs H19–H25 and AC01 in the preceding research branch at commit cfe90bb1dec157966f850d21f941d7f86385acaa. The Python collector read each saved JSON receipt and hashed it, then queried the corresponding GitHub research PR state and review records. The scorer retained unknown values as null. We compared ordinary and optimized Python outputs byte for byte and independently recomputed observed coverage counts in SQLite. Ten unit tests cover missing/duplicate records, invalid minutes, boolean-as-cost, inconsistent merge status, invalid acceptance, and bounds. These tests validate accounting logic rather than the scientific claims in each artifact.

![Chart: evidence availability across eight sampled topics](/assets/research/ac02-coverage.svg)

| Evidence | Observed |
|---|---:|
| Saved research receipt | 8/8 |
| Merged research PR | 0/8 |
| PR approved review records | 0 |
| Recorded independent acceptance | 0/8 |
| Active human minutes in selected receipt | 0/8 |
| Expert human baseline minutes in selected receipt | 0/8 |
| Attributed actual USD cost in selected receipt | 0/8 |

The first five and last three cases were summarized separately with the same frozen scoring rule. Both groups show missing human-time and cost fields. This is not a prospectively held-out benchmark or blinded inter-rater study: all eight topics were already known. Absence of those exact fields does not establish that humans did no work, that no reviewer exists outside the PR, or that the costs were zero.

Two topics contained direct Manager diagnostics. On both, Manager's Brier score failed to beat the specified prior baseline. We explicitly count these negative outcomes rather than selecting favorable numbers. That is compatible with successful research execution: learning that a candidate fails can be scientifically useful. It is not compatible with a claim of model improvement.

## Interpretation and next step

The observed artifacts establish that research evidence was recorded, but the strict autonomy rate is unidentified: the bound is 0–100%. We cannot estimate acceleration relative to human experts without timed comparisons, nor infer return on research investment without actual expenditure and outcomes. Our sample excludes unrecorded and abandoned tasks, and is a convenience sample from one research sequence. It is not representative of the whole company. No new human study, model training, official benchmark run or product release was performed here.

For Anicca, the immediate improvement is to add this evidence contract to ManagerBench and use it prospectively, not to invent a high autonomy score. A fixed research queue, independent verification, human labor and cost telemetry, and all failed attempts should accompany each model or product change. The goal is more reproducible knowledge and better products per unit of resource, with transparent limits and retained safeguards.

Reproduction: run the audit against the pinned receipt manifest; ordinary and optimized Python should agree, then run the ten unit tests. The artifact, independent review, broader task census, human-time measurement and publication gates are tracked in [AC02 issue #790](https://github.com/Daisuke134/anicca-ops/issues/790). The source links above describe external methodologies; our audit is a separate diagnostic, not a reproduction of their indexes.
